note: No Level 2 metrics. The task's only metric was the rate of higher-expected-value choices, which treats risk neutrality as correct; expected-utility theory, the normative standard for risky choice, does not fix risk attitude, so a risk-averse agent choosing the sure option makes no error. The pattern is tested at Level 3 (above_chance_ev_optimal, construct_type bias). The source-study rate remains in scoring/human_baselines/marbles_risk.json for reference.
